subject.title: RFC 0009: align Hosted Feed v1 specifications

question: Should RFC 0009 be approved as the normative compatibility and signed-feed trust contract before the linked OpenClaw and ClawHub implementations provide synchronized interoperability evidence?
rationale: The PR fixes permanent wire and security boundaries, and static review cannot determine whether maintainers intend to lock those choices before the implementation stack converges.

options.title: Require synchronized proof
options.body: Keep the RFC in review until linked implementations run shared fixtures covering wire compatibility, pagination, deltas, identity binding, and trust failures.

options.title: Approve the specification first
options.body: Accept the RFC as the controlling contract now and require implementation branches to conform afterward, explicitly owning correction risk.

recommendation.title: Require synchronized proof
recommendation.body: Keep the RFC in review until linked implementations run shared fixtures covering wire compatibility, pagination, deltas, identity binding, and trust failures.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and repeatedly developed RFC 0009 and are best positioned to coordinate the specification with its implementation track.
